The positioning line, a Hannover online marketing agency for the AI era pioneering GEO and LLM readability alongside SEO, performance marketing, online PR and Wikipedia PR, decodes as a search and PR agency that has moved its front door to generative engines. The headline claim, quoted as a claim, is that it is DACH's most visible online marketing agency and a top three SEO agency there; the record also lists it as co-organiser of SEAcamp, described as one of Germany's leading performance marketing and tracking conferences.

Three lines score 3: AI Search / GEO (title and H1 target visibility in the AI era, the meta leads with GEO), Content & Digital PR (PR tops the service list, it claims Wikipedia PR pioneer status, the case pages name Taxi Deutschland and Wertgarantie PR work) and SEO (a deep SEO menu from audits to link building). Paid Search and Paid Social score 2: the about page lists Google Ads, GEA, Amazon and LinkedIn Ads, and the Tamaris case maximises ROAS with dynamic product ads on Meta, LinkedIn, XING, TikTok and Pinterest. Proprietary products on record: the LLM-Readability-Score (LLM-Readability-Check), a Wikidata Connector and Brand-Kontext-Optimierung. No partners are listed.

AI posture: it sells itself as a GEO pioneer, with LLM readability scoring credited to Olaf Kopp, brand context optimisation, Generative Engine Advertising and Agentic Commerce Optimization, backed by GEO webinars, studies and checklists. Pricing signals: a free initial consultation, a free LLM readability check for two URLs, Wikipedia PR as fixed price packages. Recent moves: none dated; news, case study detail and jobs are empty; the only dated activity is LinkedIn event ads for a 50 seat Microsoft advertising meetup in Hannover. Conspicuously absent for a search agency: AI Automation, Web & Product, Local and Programmatic all score 0, and the Horus move read finds no feed, schema or entity work although the proprietary list names a Wikidata Connector.
clients:
The record lists a mixed client type, verticals of fashion and footwear ecommerce, automotive (employer branding), taxi and mobility, warranty and repair, B2B and ecommerce, and a home market of Hannover, Germany, with the DACH claim on the homepage. The book on record is four names, all case study evidence, 1 observed and 3 named only, and the observed mix is paid performance at 100%.

Tamaris is the observed client: its case study slug reads mit dpas den roas maximieren, a paid performance need (N2) met with dynamic product ads. Volkswagen Group Services carries a case study URL but no title, so it is coded named only; the verticals list carries automotive (employer branding) and the service list Digital Recruiting & Employer Branding, so an employer branding engagement is the likely read, inferred, moderate confidence. Taxi Deutschland and Wertgarantie Beteiligungen are also coded named only, but the Content & Digital PR evidence note names both as PR cases and their slugs read gestaltung der oeffentlichen meinung and studienkommunikation, so PR, reputation and content (N12) is the need the slugs point to, even though the computed read did not assign it.

No client on this book appears on another tracked agency's book; the shared count is 0. Three of four clients are names only, which the openings flag as thin evidence.

openings:
The strongest opening is the AI line's own house: Aufgesang sells AI visibility as a GEO pioneer and publishes no llms.txt, with 15 AI topic URLs in its sitemap and 0 updated in 90 days. A rival whose own site is machine readable and publishing can very likely lead with that contradiction (moderate confidence). Falsifier: an llms.txt on aufgesang.de and 90 day sitemap updates at the next compile.

No ads tested inside AI assistants show, so the first agency in its segment with results there sets the price. The three named only clients are questions to ask; its outcome pricing and free checks make a price only pitch unlikely to work.
